subject: HW Eval Playbook & MAP — performance plan, MIG vs full GPU, sizing
messages:
From: Sara Dawson <sara.dawson@acme.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: HW eval playbook + MAP: performance plan & timelines

Karthik —

Thanks for taking this on. We'd like Redwood to provide a mutual action plan (MAP) for a performance evaluation ahead of our procurement decision. High level asks:

- A benchmark plan and results that cover latency (p50/p95), TTFT (time-to-first-token), sustained throughput under target concurrency, and cold-start characteristics.
- Comparative matrix across A100, H100, and L40S, including MIG vs full-GPU tradeoffs (e.g., 1g/2g/3g MIG slices).
- Sizing guidance for a production fleet to meet ~120 qps peak for our chat + reranking path.
- Recommended canary timeline and any risks/rollback strategies.

We need enough detail to include in our internal evaluation packet for procurement and infra. Target close window: end of April if the MAP + preliminary numbers look good. If you can provide a clear timeline and a short set of deliverables we can push internally.

Can you also include suggested measurement harness (models, sequence lengths, prompt mix) — we'll need to reproduce results on our side.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Dawson
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Corporation

P.S. happy to schedule a quick sync this week if helpful.
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Sara Dawson <sara.dawson@acme.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HW eval playbook + MAP: performance plan & timelines

Sara — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a first-pass HW Eval Playbook and the bench-configs we propose. Short summary below; full deliverables are in the attachment (redwood_hw_eval_playbook_v1.pdf).

Proposed MAP & deliverables (high level):
- Week 0 (this week): scope & sign-off on test cases, dataset prompts, and success criteria. Lead: Acme (approve scope), Redwood (define bench harness).
- Days 1–3: Controlled microbenchmarks (single model, various sequence lengths) to generate p50/p95, TTFT, and per-GPU throughput.
- Days 4–10: End-to-end workload runs (chat + rerank mix) under increasing concurrency profiles (1, 8, 32, 128 concurrent request workers) to map throughput vs latency.
- Day 11: MIG vs full-GPU comparison runs, including 1g/2g/3g slice configs on A100/H100 where available.
- Day 14: Preliminary results delivery + short readout.
- Week 3: Final report with recommended fleet sizing and canary plan.

Benchmark matrix (example):
- Models: open-llama-7b / open-llama-13b / acme-tuned-13b (if you provide weights); tokens: 32/128/512; prompt mix: 60% chat, 30% single-turn generate, 10% rerank.
- Metrics: p50/p95 latency, TTFT, tokens/sec, effective qps at latency SLO (p95 <= 300ms), and GPU utilization.
- Fleet sizing: we will produce a recommendation mapping qps -> GPU count for each HW family and for different quantization profiles (fp16, int8 where supported).

MIG guidance: we'll run MIG on both A100 and H100 and report per-slice throughput. Early expectation: H100 full GPU gives best raw throughput for large models; MIG can improve cost-efficiency for small 7b workloads but may increase p95 under bursty concurrency. We'll quantify.

Timeline ask / next steps:
- Please confirm scope by EOD Thu (2027-04-01).
- We'll run initial microbenchmarks and have preliminary numbers by Fri (2027-04-08).
- Schedule readout the week of 2027-04-11; final report available by 2027-04-22.

Links & references: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-acme-eval (bench configs + scripts), HubSpot deal HSP-89812.

Attachments: redwood_hw_eval_playbook_v1.pdf, bench-configs.yaml

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Karthik —

This looks good. Two requests before we kick off:

1) Please make sure MIG experiments include 2x-H100 NVLink topology (we believe our target environment will use multi-GPU NVLink for cross-GPU KV cache placement).
2) We require a short compliance snapshot for data-handling during the bench (logs, retention) — attaching our questionnaire (acme_compliance_questionnaire.pdf).

If you can share preliminary p50/p95 + TTFT numbers for the 7b/13b picks within 3 business days (so we can present to procurement on 04/12), we’ll expedite approvals and try to meet the end-of-April close.

Also, procurement asked for a simple canary plan: 1% traffic -> 10% -> 25% over two weeks; please include rollback triggers in the final plan.

Best,
Sara

Sara — agreed on the two asks. Confirming schedule and commitments below (aligned to MAP):

- Scope sign-off by 2027-04-01: pending (please confirm scope in reply).
- Preliminary microbenchmark deliverable: 2027-04-08 (CSV + short summary). Will include p50/p95, TTFT, tokens/sec across A100/H100/L40S for 7b and 13b models and for MIG slices (1g/2g/3g where applicable).
- NVLink topology: we'll include a 2x-H100 NVLink config and highlight KV-cache implications.
- Compliance: Redwood will provide a bench-run data handling note (logs retained 7 days by default, CI redact rules applied) and complete the questionnaire sections you flagged.
- Final report & canary plan: 2027-04-22 with recommended fleet sizing. Preliminary sizing note: for your 120 qps peak target and our baseline 13b profile, expect ~12–18 H100 full GPUs depending on quantization and traffic burst profile; we'll refine with actual numbers in the prelim CSV.

Meeting: I booked a 30-min readout for 2027-04-08 10:00 PT (invite sent).

Attachments (to be delivered with the 04/08 packet): prelim-results-20270408.csv, readout-slide-deck.pdf (link in drive).

If procurement can commit to the MAP sign-off, we’ll prioritize the NVLink runs.

Thanks — looking forward to the readout.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
